review_description: Altogether very stressful experience. Firstly the date got moved and information flow was unreliable. We had to keep chasing. Installation in November 2018.On installation day an unmarked van appeared with (apart from 1) non-English speaking people. Australian Powervault employees had been promised.A major mistake happened with the wiring and an engineer had to come back a few days later to rewire the inverter.It took several attempts to get the computer link to the Fronius inverter going so that we could monitor our in/output. Two nice employees tried their best to rectify it.It took another 2 months to get the smart meter installed to finally benefit from rebates for power sent to the grid.Finally we heard a few weeks later that Powervault had ceased trading, which was a big worry. However, Mark B took over part of the business and promised to honour the warranties we had been given.The system has worked well so far.

For some reason the 20 x 310 watt Jinko panels were replaced with Jinko 18 x 360 watt  panels boosting the system from 6.2 kw to 6.4 kw.  It also makes it easier to add more panels if needed.  The company says the substitution was to "ensure smoother operation of the system" but I suspect it was really a stock in hand problem. No matter, I get the benefit.  The installation isn't fined as to come is still the inverter (A Fronius Sumo). The unit delivered was 5kw so It was sent back for the 6kw. The Fronius smart meter  is also yet to come.For your general info:  An Energy Australia representative told me that we could no longer change our tariff from ToU to a standard or fixed rate because the retailer would no longer do it.  Very odd.  The retailer told me that was "rubbish". Another Energy Australia representative (very cluey and obviously a higher rank) told me that it could be done but advised very strongly against it. It would cost us a lot more money.  Our recent bill is for $811 and we used less current that the same period 2017. The same period last year was $660.  My intention is to leave things the way we are and run with the solar system (when it is completed next week, hopefully) for one more quarter (for comparison reasons). After that, change to a fixed rate.   There's only two of us and we have solar hot water on a dedicated off-peak circuit.  I would like to say a big thank you too Solar Quote- for the invaluable knowledge and help.

Solar Australia were great too however when I went to order the system from them I couldn't get through. I left a couple of messages then the mailbox was full and I could not get a response or a return phone call.  I decided to try power vault again to see if they would do a better price and they did so I went with them.

I found the quotes offered from the suppliers through SolarQuotes to be most useful in establishing baseline information on cost, quality and system variation. In the end I received a competitive price from a local supplier and used the knowledge gained to provide the system I wanted. Thanks SolarQuotes for the service provided it made the process far more certain and allowed me to discuss design options with suppliers with confidence.
Very responsive and knowledgeable sales staff
Installation delayed because of Christmas period and lack of availability of Inverter
I haven't got it installed yet as we're waiting for grid approval which takes a few weeks. Looking forward to it!

We chose PowerVault Newcastle as recommended by your Solar Quotes website. Your website provided all the information we needed, so when they came to do our quote we had a good idea of what we were looking for. PowerVault has exceeded our expectations and I would recommend them to anyone.

Do not use this company for your solar installation if you wish to avoid delays, poor communication and sloppy administration. I received an initial estimate by email and this was followed up by a visit from a representative who was knowledgeable and informative. I was also informed that if I signed up before the end of November 2017 I would not come under the freedom of choice of installer that started on 1st December and that they could install the meter. This turned out to be untrue. Following the initial visit, all of my subsequent emails requesting information as to why installation was delayed, went unanswered.Their engineers showed me a roof plan but days before this it was changed apparently at the request of the installers. No effort was made to contact me to discuss this and as a result I have some unsightly panels on one roof.Installation was finally completed 3 months after I signed the contract but no reason was given. I then had to wait a further 3 months for the meter to be connected by Energy Australia. This may have taken longer had I not contacted Energy Ausralia myself to find that Powervault had given them a wrong telephone number, that they had been using to try and contact me regarding installation.I find it unacceptable that it should take 6 months to get a working solar system installed. This was responsible for me not saving on the cost of electricity during summer where generation is highest and the cost of running air conditioning and pool pumps the greatest.When I made my final payment I requested a receipt for this and some 6 weeks later I am still waiting to receive itThe only positive in the story was the quality of the service provided by the installers who did a great job and communicated well. Thanks to Nathan and Steve of Kraft Electrical Newcastle. I have used this company for subsequent unrelated electrical work

Panels are on roof but waiting on meter update.  Thanks for your assistance it was greatly appreciated.  I used your info and comparison sheet to campare quotes. Your info was a great help in selecting which panels and inverter to buy. I felt I was better able to make an informed choice due to your assistance.I have recommended your website to others.I will contact you again when I'm looking for a battery system.Thanks
